subject: general
question: Pure ghee costs ₹86/kg. After adulterating it with vegetable oil costing ₹43/kg, a dishonest shopkeeper sells the mixture at the rate of ₹80/kg, thereby making a profit of 60%. In what ratio does he mix the two?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of mixture = Selling Price ÷ (1 + Profit%) = 80 ÷ 1.6 = ₹50/kg

Using the Alligation method to find the ratio of Vegetable Oil to Pure Ghee:

Ratio = (CP of Ghee − CP of Mixture) : (CP of Mixture − CP of Veg Oil)

Ratio = (86 − 50) : (50 − 43) = 36 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 36 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of Pure Ghee = ₹86/kg

Cost Price (CP) of Vegetable Oil = ₹43/kg

Selling Price (SP) of the mixture = ₹80/kg

Profit on selling the mixture = 60%

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Quantity of Cheaper : Quantity of Dearer = (Dearer CP − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cheaper CP)
